full_text_zh:
[P1] 彩虹的尽头
A·H·本杰明 文 约翰·本德尔·布朗耐罗 图 汪芳 译
东方娃娃
绘本版

[P2] “哇！”獾和狐狸喘着气说，
“好美啊！”
一道明亮的清晰的彩虹像宝石
项链一样挂在天上。

[P3] 獾和狐狸盯着明亮的颜色看呆了。
獾说：“你知道吗，彩虹的尽头有宝贝呢！”
狐狸问：“什么宝贝？”
“不知道。”獾说，“但我想它应该是金的，或者银的，或者宝石的，它能让你变得永远永远都富有！”
“我们去找这个宝贝吧！”狐狸兴奋地叫起来。
于是，他们朝附近的树林出发了。

[P4] 当他们赶路时，满脑子想的都是宝贝。
它会是什么样子的呢？是大还是小？是什么颜色？
就在这时，他们看到了松鼠，他正坐在一堆橡果前面。
“我的宝贝。”他自言自语着，“我最美的宝贝啊！”

[P5] 獾和狐狸跑向松鼠。
“走开！”松鼠叫起来，“你们不许偷我的宝贝！
“这不是宝贝，”狐狸说，“这只是一堆橡果嘛。”
“对我来说，宝贝就是冬天的食物。还有什么比这更重要呢？”松鼠回答。
“哦，我们要找的是真正的宝贝！”獾一边说，一边和狐狸继续向前走去。

[P6] 很快，獾和狐狸来到了一条小河边。在草丛中，他们看到了鸭妈妈。
“我的小宝贝！”鸭妈妈呼唤着，
“你在哪儿啊？”
獾和狐狸觉得很奇怪。
“你在找宝贝吗？”他们问。
“是啊，在找我的小宝贝。”鸭妈妈回答，“哦，看那，
他在那儿呢！”

[P7] 一只金黄色的、毛茸茸的小鸭子扇着翅膀
“扑啦扑啦”跑过来了。
鸭妈妈一把把他揽到了翅膀底下。
“别再这样乱跑了，”她温柔地说，“你让我好担心，我的宝贝！”
獾和狐狸被弄糊涂了，他们问：“这就是你的宝贝？”
“当然啦，”鸭妈妈自豪地笑着，“我爱我的宝宝，胜过这个世界上的任何东西。对我来说，他就是我的宝贝啊！不是吗，我的小宝贝？我们回家吧。”

[P8] 獾和狐狸继续向前赶，他们好想快点找到
彩虹尽头的那个宝贝。他们急急忙忙爬上一个小
山坡，看见兔子爷爷坐在那儿。

“嗨！”兔子爷爷向他们打招呼。
“您好啊！”獾和狐狸说，“我们在找宝贝。”
“宝贝啊，”兔子爷爷点点头说，“我有许多呢。”
“真的？在那儿？”獾和狐狸问。

[P9] 兔子爷爷轻轻拍拍自己的头，说：“在这儿。我的回忆就是我的宝贝，它们让我快乐！”
“‘回忆’是什么？”獾问。
“它们是你记得的所有过去的事情。”兔子爷爷说，“比如你做过的事情，你去过的地方，你爱过的朋友……将来有一天，你们现在所做的这件事情也会成为你们很宝贝的回忆喔。祝你们快乐，小家伙们！”
“再见！”獾和狐狸说完，就顺着山坡的另一边滑下去了。

[P10] 就在这时，大片大片的黑云布满了天空，
彩虹消失了。雨越来越大，獾和狐狸不得不躲到了树阴下。
“到现在，我们还没有找到宝贝呢。”獾伤心地说。

[P11] 在他们等待雨停的时候，他们想起了松鼠——他有足够的食物吃，多开心啊！

他们还想起了鸭妈妈和她心爱的宝宝……

兔子爷爷也很幸福，因为他有他的回忆。

他们都有了属于自己的宝贝……也许宝贝本来就不是金的，不是银的，也不是宝石的，而是一些很特别的东西，它会让你变得非常非常开心。

狐狸看着獾，獾看着狐狸……

[P12] “你 是我的宝贝！”獾跳起来说。
“你也是我的宝贝！”狐狸说。他拉
起獾的手转起了圈儿。
他们开始笑啊跳啊，直到累得不能
再跳了！

[P13] 雨停了，太阳又出来了。两个朋友开心地
走回了家。在他们身后远远的地方，一道新的彩
虹挂上了天空，但他们俩谁也没有看见。
full_text_en:
[P1] The End of the Rainbow
A.H. Benjamin, text; John B. Brown, illustrations; translated by Wang Fang
Oriental Baby
Picture Book Edition

[P2] "Wow!" the badger and the fox panted,
"How beautiful!"
A bright, clear rainbow hung in the sky like a necklace of gemstones.

[P3] The badger and the fox stared at the bright colors, spellbound.
Badger said, “You know, there’s treasure at the end of the rainbow!”
Fox asked, “What kind of treasure?”
“I don’t know,” said Badger, “but I think it should be made of gold, or silver, or jewels—it could make you rich forever and ever!”
“Let’s go find this treasure!” the fox called out excitedly.
So, they set off toward the nearby woods.

[P4] As they hurried along, all they could think about was treasure.
What would it look like? Big or small? What color?
Just then, they saw the squirrel, sitting in front of a pile of acorns.
"My treasure," he murmured to himself, "my most beautiful treasure!"

[P5] The badger and the fox ran towards the squirrel.
"Go away!" the squirrel cried, "You're not allowed to steal my treasure!"
"This isn't treasure," said the fox, "It's just a pile of acorns."
"For me, treasure is food for winter. What could be more important than this?" the squirrel replied.
"Oh, we're looking for real treasure!" said the badger, as he and the fox continued on their way.

[P6] Soon, the badger and the fox arrived at a small river. In the grass, they saw a duck mother.
"My little treasure!" the duck mother called out,
"Where are you?"
The badger and the fox felt very strange.
"Are you looking for treasure?" they asked.
"Yes, I'm looking for my little treasure," the duck mother replied, "Oh, look there,
he's over there!"

[P7] A golden, fluffy little duck flapped its wings
"Flap flap" and ran over.
The duck mother quickly pulled him under her wing.
"Don't run around like that anymore," she said gently, "You make me so worried, my darling!"
The badger and the fox were confused. They asked, "Is this your treasure?"
"Of course!" the duck mother smiled proudly, "I love my baby more than anything in the world. To me, he is my treasure! Isn't that right, my little darling? Let's go home."

[P8] The badger and the fox continued on their way, eager to find
the treasure at the end of the rainbow. They hurried up a small
hill and saw Grandpa Rabbit sitting there.

"Hi!" Grandpa Rabbit waved to them.
"Hello!" the badger and the fox said, "We're looking for treasure."
"Treasure?" Grandpa Rabbit nodded, "I have many."
"Really? Where?" the badger and the fox asked.

[P9] Grandpa Rabbit gently patted his head and said, "Right here. My memories are my treasures; they make me happy!"
"What are 'memories'?" asked the badger.
"They are all the things you remember from the past," said Grandpa Rabbit. "Like the things you've done, the places you've been, the friends you've loved... One day, the very thing you're doing now will become a precious memory for you. Wishing you happiness, little ones!"
"Goodbye!" said the badger and fox, then slid down the other side of the hill.

[P10] At this moment, large, dark clouds filled the sky,
the rainbow disappeared. The rain grew heavier, and the badger and fox had to take shelter under the tree.
"Up until now, we haven't found the treasure," the badger said sadly.

[P11] While waiting for the rain to stop, they remembered the squirrel—he had enough food to eat, how happy he was!

They also remembered the duck mother and her beloved baby...

Grandpa Rabbit was also very happy, because he had his memories.

They each had their own treasure... perhaps treasure is not made of gold, not silver, nor gemstones, but something very special that makes you extremely happy.

The fox looked at the badger, and the badger looked at the fox...

[P12] "You are my treasure!" the badger jumped up and said.
"You are my treasure too!" the fox said. He took the badger's hand and spun around.
They began laughing and jumping until they were too tired to jump anymore!

[P13] The rain stopped, and the sun came out again. The two friends happily
walked back home. In the distance behind them, a new rainbow
appeared in the sky, but neither of them saw it.
full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页为绘本《彩虹的尽头》的封面，展示了狐狸和獾在彩虹下的草地握手，下方标注了作者、绘者、译者及出版社信息。
[P2] 獾和狐狸站在草地上，抬头仰望天空中出现的一道明亮清晰的彩虹，感到非常惊叹和赞美。
[P3] 獾和狐狸被彩虹吸引，獾提到彩虹尽头有宝贝，狐狸兴奋地提议去找，于是他们一起朝树林出发。
[P4] 獾和狐狸在森林里赶路，满脑子想着彩虹尽头的宝贝，这时他们看到松鼠正坐在一堆橡果前，自言自语地称橡果为自己的宝贝。
[P5] 獾和狐狸在森林里遇到松鼠，松鼠守护着一堆橡果并称其为宝贝，狐狸认为那只是橡果，獾则坚持要寻找真正的宝贝，于是他们继续向前走去。
[P6] 獾和狐狸在河边遇到鸭妈妈，她正在呼唤自己的小宝贝，獾和狐狸误以为她在找彩虹尽头的宝贝，感到奇怪。
[P7] 獾和狐狸在河边遇到鸭妈妈，她正呼唤并保护自己的小鸭子，称其为宝贝。獾和狐狸误以为小鸭子是彩虹尽头的宝贝，感到困惑，鸭妈妈则解释说自己的孩子就是她最珍贵的宝贝。
[P8] 獾和狐狸在寻找彩虹尽头的宝贝途中，爬上一个小山坡，遇到了坐在那里的兔子爷爷。他们向兔子爷爷问好，并询问他是否知道宝贝在哪里，兔子爷爷表示自己有许多宝贝。
[P9] 獾和狐狸在山坡上遇到兔子爷爷，兔子爷爷告诉他们自己的宝贝是回忆，并解释了回忆的含义。随后，獾和狐狸向兔子爷爷道别，顺着山坡滑下去继续他们的旅程。
[P10] 獾和狐狸在寻找彩虹尽头的宝贝途中，天空突然乌云密布，彩虹消失，大雨倾盆，他们只好躲到树下避雨，獾感到伤心，因为还没有找到宝贝。
[P11] 獾和狐狸在树下避雨时，回忆起之前遇到的松鼠、鸭妈妈和兔子爷爷，意识到每个人心中的宝贝各不相同，最终领悟到宝贝是能带来快乐的特别事物。
[P12] 獾和狐狸互相称对方为宝贝，开心地手拉手转圈，然后一起笑啊跳啊，直到累得不能再跳。
[P13] 雨停后，獾和狐狸开心地走回家，身后天空出现了一道新彩虹，但他们没有注意到。
[P14] 画面中，獾和狐狸并肩走在草地上，狐狸在前，獾在后，两者都面带微笑，似乎正愉快地回家。
